facts.fact: The Adwave article 'Your Business Address Is More Than Just Mail' was published on March 7, 2026.

The article gives a 15-mile radius as one example of how a service-area business (such as a plumber or electrician) might define its service area; it is an illustrative example, not a platform requirement.
facts.quote: This might be a **15-mile** radius or a specific list of zip codes.

facts.fact: The page predicts there will be 3.41 billion IPv4 addresses in use globally by 2026.
facts.quote: By 2026, it's predicted there will be **3.41 billion** IPv4 addresses in use around the globe

facts.fact: The page states that the United States holds 1.23 billion IPv4 addresses.
facts.quote: the United States holds a staggering **1.23 billion** of these addresses

facts.fact: The page states that the United States' share of global IPv4 addresses is roughly 36% of the world's total.
facts.quote: that's roughly **36%** of the world's total

facts.fact: The page states that customer data decays at a rate of over 2% per month, without citing a source.
facts.quote: customer data decays at a rate of over **2%** per month

facts.fact: The page states that more than 20% of a customer address list could be out of date within a single year.
facts.quote: more than **20%** of your list could be out of date within a single year

facts.fact: Adwave states that its campaigns start from $30 per day.
The page projects the global internet audience to reach 6 billion people by 2026.
facts.quote: By 2026, the global internet audience is projected to hit **6 billion people**

facts.fact: The page states that 2.21 billion people are still offline.
According to Potaroo.net data cited by the page, the pool of available IPv4 addresses for transfer has fallen by 58% since 2015 (third-party figure, not Adwave's).
facts.quote: the pool of available IPv4 addresses for transfer has plummeted by **58%** since 2015

facts.fact: Adwave states that it relies on verified TV viewing data rather than IP-dependent digital methods.
facts.quote: relies on verified TV viewing data instead of IP-dependent digital methods

facts.fact: Adwave states that it never targets an individual person or a specific household address.
facts.quote: Reputable providers like **Adwave** never target an individual person or a specific household **address**.

facts.fact: Adwave states that it uses address data in an aggregated, anonymous way to define a geographic targeting area such as a neighborhood, set of zip codes, or radius around a business.
facts.quote: we use address data in an aggregated, anonymous way to define a geographic targeting area

facts.fact: Adwave states that a campaign can be launched using only the advertiser's own business address, with no customer address list required.
facts.quote: You can launch a highly effective campaign with just your own business address.

facts.fact: Adwave states that having a list of past customer addresses is not a requirement to get started with address-based TV advertising.
facts.quote: it's definitely not a requirement to get started.
